{{short description|American mathematician}}

[[File:Jeff Kahn.jpg|thumb|220px|Jeff Kahn at [[Oberwolfach Research Institute for Mathematics|Oberwolfach]] in 2008]]
'''Jeffry Ned Kahn''' is a professor of mathematics at [[Rutgers University]] notable for his work in [[combinatorics]].

==Education==
Kahn received his Ph.D. from [[Ohio State University]] in 1979 after completing his dissertation under his advisor [[Dijen K. Ray-Chaudhuri]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy |id=9979}}</ref>

==Research==
In 1980, he showed the importance of the [[bundle theorem]] for ovoidal [[Möbius plane]]s.<ref>''Inversive planes satisfying the bundle theorem'', Journal Combinatorial Theory, Serie A, Vol.29, 1980, p. 1-19</ref> In 1993, together with [[Gil Kalai]], he disproved [[Borsuk's conjecture]].<ref>{{citation|first1=Jeff|last1=Kahn|first2=Gil|last2=Kalai|author2-link=Gil Kalai|arxiv=math.MG/9307229 |title=A counterexample to Borsuk's conjecture|journal=[[Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society]] |volume=29|year=1993|pages=60–62|doi=10.1090/S0273-0979-1993-00398-7|mr=1193538|s2cid=119647518}}.</ref> In 1996, he was awarded the [[Pólya Prize (SIAM)]].

==Awards and honors==
He was an invited speaker at the 1994 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Zurich.{{cn|date=May 2022}}

In 2012, he was awarded the [[Fulkerson Prize]] (jointly with Anders Johansson and [[Van H. Vu]]) for determining the threshold of edge density above which a [[random graph]] can be covered by disjoint copies of a given smaller graph.<ref>{{cite journal | title=Factors in random graphs | author=Anders Johansson, Jeff Kahn, and [[Van H. Vu]] | journal=Random Structures and Algorithms | year=2008 | volume=33 | issue=1 | pages=1–28 | doi=10.1002/rsa.20224| arxiv=0803.3406 | s2cid=14337643 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ams.org/profession/prizes-awards/ams-prizes/fulkerson-prize |title=Delbert Ray Fulkerson Prize |publisher= [[American Mathematical Society]] (AMS) |access-date= 3 Jan 2013 }}</ref> Also in 2012, he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2013-01-27.</ref>
